services.name: SOP Development
services.summary: Standard Operating Procedures that bring consistency and clarity.
services.intro: Clear procedures turn the way you work from personal habit into an organizational system. We develop SOPs, authority matrices and documentation standards that define who owns what, who decides and what must be escalated, so knowledge stays in the organization even when people leave. Not every problem needs another SOP, so we simplify and clarify before we add.
problems: Decisions depend on who you know, not the system
Nobody knows who has the authority to approve
Knowledge lives on employees' laptops and leaves with them
The same task is done differently by every team
Too many approval layers slow every decision
Responsibilities overlap and accountability is missing
examples: A procurement manager placed a direct supply order without the procurement committee, and when a quality problem appeared nobody took responsibility. Where authority is granted through a written delegation system, the result is flow, clarity and mutual trust.

A client was asked for technical support eight years after project completion, but the project team had left with no handover, archive or central documentation. Governance, documentation standards and centralized systems keep that knowledge inside the organization.

services.name: Workflow Design
services.summary: Efficient workflows that simplify operations and reduce errors.
services.intro: Behind every simple customer experience there is a business process, and that process should be designed to be complex but controlled. We map how work actually flows, question every step, and redesign workflows that give teams speed while giving management visibility and control. Technology automates a workflow, but it does not redesign it, so we design first and digitize second.
problems: A simple request waits days for email approvals
Every case follows the same heavy review process
Information is scattered and staff waste time searching
Handovers between departments cause delays and errors
Quotations take days to prepare
New systems were added on top of broken processes
examples: A company digitizing its procurement process questioned each step with a cross-functional team, redesigned the workflow and reduced approvals from nine to five, rather than simply digitizing waste.

Without a defined workflow, a LinkedIn post can loop through Draft, Email, Waiting, Reminder and Revision and take three days. A segmented flow from content brief to authorized approval gives speed, consistency, control and accountability.

services.name: Business Process Improvement
services.summary: Improve performance, eliminate waste and create more value.
services.intro: Improvement should not start with "What should we buy?" but with "How should we work?". We identify hidden waste, analyze processes and find the root causes behind repeated issues, then remove, simplify, standardize and automate. The goal is not to cut resources blindly but to free them for higher-value work.
problems: Repeated issues keep coming back
The first answer to every problem is hiring
Reports are produced that nobody uses
Departments duplicate each other's work
Skilled people spend time on low-value tasks
Targets are set without knowing how to reach them
examples: Instead of hiring three more customer service staff, a company redesigned the workflow, clarified responsibilities, centralized information, removed unnecessary approvals and automated repetitive tasks, so the existing team could handle more with less effort.

A building materials company aiming for 20% more revenue analyzed its growth levers instead of pushing salespeople harder, including simplifying quotations from three days to one and improving inventory planning, so revenue could grow without increasing the sales team.

services.name: Training & Development
services.summary: Practical training that builds skills and drives real results.
services.intro: Knowledge creates value only when it is shared and applied. We run practical training programmes and leadership workshops built on real examples, from conflict resolution and emotional intelligence to business planning, governance and value-based selling. We help leaders and teams build the mindset, tools and discipline for sustainable performance.
problems: Top performers promoted into management without leadership skills
New managers spend months before creating value
Conflicts turn personal and drain the team
Salespeople discount too quickly to close deals
Managers treat business planning as a finance task
Gossip and office politics replace open communication
deliverables: Governance and authority workshops for leaders
Emotional intelligence and dialogue skills workshops
Coaching based on real performance gaps
examples: A new Sales Manager followed a 30-60-90 Day Plan instead of pushing sales from day one: he learned the business, identified slow quotations and weak follow-up, redesigned the process and coached the team, and quotation time dropped by 50%.

A company promoted its top performers to managerial roles, and within a year performance dropped, conflicts increased and morale fell, because communication skills, emotional intelligence and the ability to develop others had been ignored.

services.name: Quality & Excellence
services.summary: Quality systems that ensure reliability and customer satisfaction.
services.intro: What gets measured gets improved, but only if you measure what matters. We design KPI frameworks and dashboards linked to strategy, and apply Lean, DMAIC, Business Excellence and data-driven methods to improve quality, customer experience and retention. Excellence is not a one-time achievement but a journey built through the right people, processes and systems.
problems: Lots of data, but no real insight
Dashboards exist that nobody uses
Only financial results are tracked, not their drivers
Service quality is inconsistent
Customers leave and nobody knows why
Teams guess at causes instead of measuring them
deliverables: Customer success KPIs and early warnings
examples: When sales were falling, a KPI dashboard showed that quotation response time had grown from 1 day to 5 days and conversion had dropped from 40% to 25%, so the company could fix the actual causes instead of asking salespeople to sell more.

A software company losing customers after six months found they had not been properly trained and support was slow. A churn reduction plan with onboarding, regular business reviews, usage monitoring and customer success KPIs increased engagement and renewals.

steps.name: Understand

steps.description: We start by understanding your strategy, customers, culture, KPIs and challenges. We meet stakeholders, visit operations and listen carefully before drawing conclusions.
activities: Review of reports, data and KPIs

steps.name: Diagnose
steps.title: Find waste and root causes
steps.description: We map how work really happens and look beyond the visible symptoms. We ask what organizational conditions are producing the results you see.
activities: Role, authority and data maturity review

steps.name: Design
steps.title: Simplify, then standardize
steps.description: Together with a cross-functional team, we redesign workflows, remove unnecessary steps and define clear roles and authority. Then we capture the new way of working in practical SOPs and governance.

steps.name: Implement
steps.title: Execute with your people
steps.description: We support implementation with a Project Champion who removes roadblocks and keeps momentum. Training and workshops build the skills your teams need to own the change.
activities: Automation and digitization of redesigned processes

steps.name: Measure
steps.title: Track what really matters
steps.description: What gets measured gets improved, so we put action-oriented KPIs and dashboards in place. Regular reviews turn information into decisions and further improvement.

steps.name: Sustain
steps.title: Make improvement a habit
steps.description: Resolution does not end with a meeting; we follow up to ensure results are sustained. We help embed governance and a culture of continuous improvement, so you can then scale on a stronger foundation.

principles.title: Remove before you add
principles.description: Before adding people, systems, meetings or approvals, ask what should be removed. Sometimes it is about stopping what should never have been done in the first place.

principles.title: Fix the system, not the people
principles.description: Instead of concluding "We have difficult employees", ask what organizational conditions are producing the behavior. When the signals change, behavior can change.

principles.title: Don't digitize waste
principles.description: Don't digitize inefficiency, don't hire around waste, don't scale what is broken. First build the right processes, then digitize them.

principles.title: What gets measured gets improved
principles.description: A good dashboard does not show everything; it shows what matters. Data tells you what happened, KPIs tell you what action to take.

principles.title: Authority should match the risk
principles.description: Governance should create clarity, not stop momentum. Give teams the authority to move fast on normal business and involve senior leadership where the risk requires it.

principles.title: Create value, and results follow
principles.description: We are here to create value; money comes as a result. When value is the priority, trust is built, teams develop and results last.

about.who_we_are: ImproFact is a business-improvement consultancy that helps organizations and individuals improve their performance from the inside out. We work with organizations that want to move from reactive problem-solving to structured improvement by reducing waste, increasing efficiency, improving quality and creating sustainable value. Our work covers SOPs and governance, workflow design, process improvement, training and development, and quality and excellence, alongside strategy, sales improvement, digital transformation and leadership development. We share what we know openly, in English and Arabic, because we believe knowledge creates value only when it is shared.
about.mission: To help organizations and individuals improve from the inside out through better processes, stronger teams and sustainable growth.
about.approach: We believe improvement should not start with "What should we buy?" but with "How should we work?". We understand before we act, look for root causes rather than blame, remove waste before adding resources, and build processes before digitizing them. Then we measure what matters and help make improvement a habit.

faq.question: Where should we start if we know performance could be better but can't pinpoint why?
faq.answer: We start by understanding your business and diagnosing where hidden waste, unclear processes or repeated issues are limiting performance. Rather than guessing, we map processes, look for root causes and use KPIs to make the real problems visible, then prioritize the improvements that create the most value.

faq.question: Does process improvement mean cutting staff?
faq.answer: No. Improvement is not about reducing resources blindly; it is about eliminating waste and freeing resources for higher-value work. Often the same team can handle more with less effort once duplicated work, unnecessary approvals and scattered information are removed.

faq.question: Should we buy a new system or start digital transformation first?
faq.answer: Adding a new system won't solve a broken process. We recommend establishing governance, SOPs and workflows first, then digitizing them, because technology automates processes but doesn't redesign them.

faq.question: Who in our organization needs to be involved?
faq.answer: Business processes affect everyone, so we work with a Project Champion who removes roadblocks and makes timely decisions, supported by a cross-functional team from the functions involved. An internal leader understands the culture while an external partner brings fresh perspective and proven methods; the best approach often combines both.

faq.question: Do you only advise, or do you also train our people?
faq.answer: Both. Alongside designing processes, SOPs and governance, we run practical training programmes and leadership workshops, covering topics such as conflict resolution, emotional intelligence, governance, business planning and value-based selling, so your teams can sustain the improvements themselves.

faq.question: Can you work with us in Arabic as well as English?
faq.answer: Yes. ImproFact shares its thinking and programmes in both English and Arabic, and our approach to culture, leadership and governance is designed to be practical in either language.
